Presented file
1. Is there something better than periodic fetching?

Only if you add infrastructure. Real push would mean a forge webhook hitting a server, which then sends a notification through FCM or UnifiedPush. That requires a server, Google services or an extra app, and forge-specific setup, so it breaks the spec. Within the spec, the best approach is cheap polling while the app is visible:

Polling while visible: while the app is on screen, it calls ls-remote every 30 seconds. That is one small HTTPS request that returns the branch tip.
Fetch only on change: it fetches only when that tip differs from the last one it fetched. An unchanged remote now costs just that one request. Previously every sync did ls-remote plus a full fetch.
Backoff when unreachable: if the remote can’t be reached, it backs off 30s → 1m → 2m → 4m → 5m and shows the existing “Sync not currently possible” notice.
No background cost: polling stops when the app leaves the screen, using repeatOnLifecycle(STARTED). Nobody is looking at it then, so it costs no battery.
Background sync is unchanged: WorkManager still syncs after each send and every 6h as a safety net. More frequent background polling wouldn’t help, because nobody sees the result until the app is opened, and opening it now triggers a sync right away.
This also explains what you saw. The “sync on open” only ran when the ViewModel was created. Returning to the app from recents with the process still alive triggered nothing, so a sync only happened when you sent something.

2. Read-only mode

Yes, it uses the same mechanism, so new posts appear by themselves while the app is open.

Turning it on: it’s a switch in Settings. Public repos need no username or token. The input box is hidden.
Separate local copy: it reads from a separate local mirror (files/mirror). Each time the remote changes, the mirror is hard-reset to the remote branch. When you change the URL or branch, the mirror is wiped.
Your diary stays separate: your own diary repo (files/repo) is never mixed with someone else’s entries and is never pushed to the followed remote. Any entries you wrote stay on the device and sync again when you turn read-only off.
Changes

GitRepo.kt:
fetch is skipped when the advertised tip equals the tracking ref.
The tracking ref is updated after a push, so your own push doesn’t cause a refetch.
sync now returns whether HEAD changed.
New mirror() and clear() functions handle read-only mode.
Diary.kt:
New mirror mode.
New refresh() for cheap polls, which skips the untracked-file scan.
New remoteChanged().
read() returns null for files removed by a sync, instead of crashing.
App.kt: separate diary and mirror instances, plus active() to pick the current one.
Settings.kt: new readOnly setting. lastError is only written when it changes.
Sync.kt: the worker syncs both the diary and the mirror (whichever isn’t active does nothing). Shared describe() helper for error messages.
MainViewModel.kt: the watch() polling loop, read-only state, and an “unreachable” flag merged into the sync status.
UI files:
MainActivity.kt runs watch() while the app is started.
ChatScreen.kt hides the input in read-only mode and shows its notices.
SettingsScreen.kt adds the read-only switch.
strings.xml has the new texts.
Tests:
DiaryTest.kt gains tests for refresh detection, read-only never pushing, the mirror following additions and deletions, clearing the mirror on remote change, and the mirror refusing writes.
ChatScreenTest.kt checks that read-only hides the input.
Docs: README.md and docs/SPEC.md are updated.
Delivery: my-stream-of-consciousness.tar.gz contains the whole project, with paths relative to the repo root. No files to delete. Leave gradlew, gradlew.bat and gradle/wrapper/ as they are: they weren’t in the dump, so they aren’t in the archive, and extracting over the repo leaves them untouched. I couldn’t build here, because Google’s Maven repo isn’t reachable from my sandbox, so let CI be the first compile.

1. OnePlus Nord N30 5G 
2. Samsung Galaxy Tab A9+ 
I used the same credentials for both 
https://github.com/kfedora/my-stream-of-consciousness
What I realized is the app only fetches when I send a new message

Ran 7 commands, shared files
1. Is there something better than periodic fetching?

Only if you add infrastructure. Real push would mean a forge webhook hitting a server, which then sends a notification through FCM or UnifiedPush. That requires a server, Google services or an extra app, and forge-specific setup, so it breaks the spec. Within the spec, the best approach is cheap polling while the app is visible:

Polling while visible: while the app is on screen, it calls ls-remote every 30 seconds. That is one small HTTPS request that returns the branch tip.
Fetch only on change: it fetches only when that tip differs from the last one it fetched. An unchanged remote now costs just that one request. Previously every sync did ls-remote plus a full fetch.
Backoff when unreachable: if the remote can’t be reached, it backs off 30s → 1m → 2m → 4m → 5m and shows the existing “Sync not currently possible” notice.
No background cost: polling stops when the app leaves the screen, using repeatOnLifecycle(STARTED). Nobody is looking at it then, so it costs no battery.
Background sync is unchanged: WorkManager still syncs after each send and every 6h as a safety net. More frequent background polling wouldn’t help, because nobody sees the result until the app is opened, and opening it now triggers a sync right away.
This also explains what you saw. The “sync on open” only ran when the ViewModel was created. Returning to the app from recents with the process still alive triggered nothing, so a sync only happened when you sent something.

2. Read-only mode

Yes, it uses the same mechanism, so new posts appear by themselves while the app is open.

Turning it on: it’s a switch in Settings. Public repos need no username or token. The input box is hidden.
Separate local copy: it reads from a separate local mirror (files/mirror). Each time the remote changes, the mirror is hard-reset to the remote branch. When you change the URL or branch, the mirror is wiped.
Your diary stays separate: your own diary repo (files/repo) is never mixed with someone else’s entries and is never pushed to the followed remote. Any entries you wrote stay on the device and sync again when you turn read-only off.
Changes

GitRepo.kt:
fetch is skipped when the advertised tip equals the tracking ref.
The tracking ref is updated after a push, so your own push doesn’t cause a refetch.
sync now returns whether HEAD changed.
New mirror() and clear() functions handle read-only mode.
Diary.kt:
New mirror mode.
New refresh() for cheap polls, which skips the untracked-file scan.
New remoteChanged().
read() returns null for files removed by a sync, instead of crashing.
App.kt: separate diary and mirror instances, plus active() to pick the current one.
Settings.kt: new readOnly setting. lastError is only written when it changes.
Sync.kt: the worker syncs both the diary and the mirror (whichever isn’t active does nothing). Shared describe() helper for error messages.
MainViewModel.kt: the watch() polling loop, read-only state, and an “unreachable” flag merged into the sync status.
UI files:
MainActivity.kt runs watch() while the app is started.
ChatScreen.kt hides the input in read-only mode and shows its notices.
SettingsScreen.kt adds the read-only switch.
strings.xml has the new texts.
Tests:
DiaryTest.kt gains tests for refresh detection, read-only never pushing, the mirror following additions and deletions, clearing the mirror on remote change, and the mirror refusing writes.
ChatScreenTest.kt checks that read-only hides the input.
Docs: README.md and docs/SPEC.md are updated.
Delivery: my-stream-of-consciousness.tar.gz contains the whole project, with paths relative to the repo root. No files to delete. Leave gradlew, gradlew.bat and gradle/wrapper/ as they are: they weren’t in the dump, so they aren’t in the archive, and extracting over the repo leaves them untouched. Ran 3 commands
Tracking down a suspend call inside a non-suspend lambda.
The build failed because of a mistake in one of the new tests: in mirrorFollowsRemoteDeletion, writer.entries() is a suspend function and I called it inside the non-suspend withClone lambda. The fix reads the path first, the same way remoteDeletionIsRespected already does. The release build had already compiled the app code before the test compile failed, and the log shows no other errors, so this is the only file that changes.

app/src/test/java/com/github/kusl/msoc/core/DiaryTest.kt

kotlin
package com.github.kusl.msoc.core

import com.github.kusl.msoc.git.GitRepo
import com.github.kusl.msoc.git.Remote
import kotlinx.coroutines.runBlocking
import org.eclipse.jgit.api.Git
import org.eclipse.jgit.lib.PersonIdent
import org.eclipse.jgit.transport.RefSpec
import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Assert.assertFalse
import org.junit.Assert.assertTrue
import org.junit.Before
import org.junit.Rule
import org.junit.Test
import org.junit.rules.TemporaryFolder
import java.io.File

class DiaryTest {
    @get:Rule
    val tmp = TemporaryFolder()

    private lateinit var remote: File
    private val other = PersonIdent("Other", "other@example.com")

    private class FakeSettings(var target: Remote?, var viewOnly: Boolean = false) : SettingsSource {
        override fun remote() = target
        override fun readOnly() = viewOnly
        override fun author() = "Tester" to "tester@example.com"
    }

    @Before
    fun setUp() {
        remote = bare("remote.git")
    }

    private fun bare(name: String) = tmp.newFolder(name).also { Git.init().setBare(true).setInitialBranch("main").setDirectory(it).call().close() }

    private fun upstream(dir: File = remote) = Remote(dir.absolutePath, "main", "", "")

    private fun device(settings: SettingsSource = FakeSettings(upstream()), mirror: Boolean = false): Diary {
        val dir = tmp.newFolder()
        return Diary(dir, GitRepo(dir, EntryNaming.DIR, EntryNaming::renamed), settings, mirror)
    }

    private fun reader(settings: FakeSettings = FakeSettings(upstream(), viewOnly = true)) = device(settings, mirror = true)

    private suspend fun Diary.texts() = entries().map { read(it.path) }.toSet()

    private fun remoteCommits() = Git.open(remote).use { it.log().call().count() }

    private fun withClone(block: (Git) -> Unit) = Git.cloneRepository().setURI(remote.absolutePath).setDirectory(tmp.newFolder()).call().use { git ->
        block(git)
        git.commit().setAuthor(other).setCommitter(other).setMessage("external").call()
        git.push().setRemote(remote.absolutePath).setRefSpecs(RefSpec("HEAD:refs/heads/main")).call()
    }

    @Test
    fun devicesConverge() = runBlocking<Unit> {
        val a = device()
        val b = device()
        a.add("one")
        b.add("two")
        a.sync()
        b.sync()
        a.sync()
        assertEquals(setOf("one", "two"), a.texts())
        assertEquals(setOf("one", "two"), b.texts())
        assertFalse(a.hasUnpushed())
        assertFalse(b.hasUnpushed())
        assertEquals(2, remoteCommits())
    }

    @Test
    fun refreshReportsOnlyRemoteChanges() = runBlocking<Unit> {
        val a = device()
        val b = device()
        a.add("one")
        a.sync()
        assertTrue(b.refresh())
        assertFalse(b.refresh())
        a.add("two")
        a.sync()
        assertTrue(b.refresh())
        assertEquals(setOf("one", "two"), b.texts())
    }

    @Test
    fun offlineEntriesArePushedLater() = runBlocking<Unit> {
        val settings = FakeSettings(null)
        val a = device(settings)
        a.add("one")
        a.add("two")
        a.sync()
        assertFalse(a.hasUnpushed())
        settings.target = upstream()
        assertTrue(a.hasUnpushed())
        a.sync()
        assertFalse(a.hasUnpushed())
        assertEquals(2, remoteCommits())
    }

    @Test
    fun remoteDeletionIsRespected() = runBlocking<Unit> {
        val a = device()
        a.add("gone")
        a.sync()
        val path = a.entries().single().path
        withClone { it.rm().addFilepattern(path).call() }
        a.add("kept")
        a.sync()
        assertEquals(setOf("kept"), a.texts())
    }

    @Test
    fun conflictingPathKeepsBothVersions() = runBlocking<Unit> {
        val a = device()
        a.add("mine")
        val path = a.entries().single().path
        withClone { git ->
            File(git.repository.workTree, path).apply { parentFile?.mkdirs() }.writeText("theirs")
            git.add().addFilepattern(path).call()
        }
        a.sync()
        assertEquals(setOf("mine", "theirs"), a.texts())
        assertEquals("theirs", a.read(path))
        assertFalse(a.hasUnpushed())
    }

    @Test
    fun readOnlyNeverPushes() = runBlocking<Unit> {
        val settings = FakeSettings(upstream(), viewOnly = true)
        val a = device(settings)
        a.add("one")
        assertFalse(a.sync())
        assertFalse(a.hasUnpushed())
        settings.viewOnly = false
        assertTrue(a.hasUnpushed())
        a.sync()
        assertEquals(1, remoteCommits())
    }

    @Test
    fun mirrorFollowsRemote() = runBlocking<Unit> {
        val writer = device()
        val mirror = reader()
        assertFalse(mirror.refresh())
        writer.add("one")
        writer.sync()
        assertTrue(mirror.refresh())
        assertEquals(setOf("one"), mirror.texts())
        assertFalse(mirror.refresh())
        writer.add("two")
        writer.sync()
        assertTrue(mirror.refresh())
        assertEquals(setOf("one", "two"), mirror.texts())
        assertFalse(mirror.hasUnpushed())
    }

    @Test
    fun mirrorFollowsRemoteDeletion() = runBlocking<Unit> {
        val writer = device()
        writer.add("gone")
        writer.sync()
        val mirror = reader()
        mirror.refresh()
        val path = writer.entries().single().path
        withClone { it.rm().addFilepattern(path).call() }
        assertTrue(mirror.refresh())
        assertTrue(mirror.entries().isEmpty())
    }

    @Test
    fun mirrorClearsWhenRemoteChanges() = runBlocking<Unit> {
        val writer = device()
        writer.add("one")
        writer.sync()
        val settings = FakeSettings(upstream(), viewOnly = true)
        val mirror = reader(settings)
        mirror.refresh()
        settings.target = upstream(bare("empty.git"))
        mirror.remoteChanged()
        assertTrue(mirror.entries().isEmpty())
        assertFalse(mirror.refresh())
        settings.target = upstream()
        mirror.remoteChanged()
        assertTrue(mirror.refresh())
        assertEquals(setOf("one"), mirror.texts())
    }

    @Test
    fun mirrorNeverWrites() = runBlocking<Unit> {
        val mirror = reader()
        assertTrue(runCatching { mirror.add("nope") }.isFailure)
    }
}
Once the tests run, CI will show whether anything else needs fixing.
